summary: Antonino Forte worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1972–1976), Hōbōgirin (~1976–1982), Scuola Italiana di Studi sull'Asia Orientale (~1982–1996), University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1989–2006), and the Italian School of East Asian Studies (1999).
Antonio T. de Nicolás was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied at Fordham University (~1968–1971) and held a post at Stony Brook University from circa 1968 to 1996.

Antonio Terrone specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University (1999–2010), supervised by Tilmann Vetter and Barend ter Haar, and also studied under Terton Tashi Gyaltsen, Tulku Tsezang Samling Rinpoche, and Ramon Prats d'Alos-Moner.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. A pupil of Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya, he earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta (~-1946), later serving there as Assistant Lecturer in Pali (~1938–1976) and directing the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (~1980–1983).
Anyen Rinpoche is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Lama Chupur and Tsara Dharmakirti Rinpoche.

Archibald Edward Gough was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Monier Monier-Williams (~1864–1866). He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1868–1878), Presidency University, Kolkata (~1878–1895), and served as Principal at Aliah University (~1881–1895).

Arindam Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed his DPhil at the University of Oxford (~1978–1982). He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Delhi (~1983–1997) and professor at the University of Hawaii (~1997–2018).

Arinde L. Jonker is an Indology scholar who completed a Research MA at Leiden University (~2016–2018). There, Jonker studied under Jonathan A. Silk and MA supervisor Peter Bisschop, and also taught Daniele Cuneo.
Aristotle C. Dy is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (~2008–2013) under the doctoral supervision of Antonello Palumbo.

Arjo Vanderjagt, a philosopher, studied at Franklin Academy, Prattsburgh Central School, and the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held positions at Radboud University (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Arlo Griffiths specializes in Indology and linguistics. After earning a PhD at Leiden University (1999–2004) under Henk Bodewitz and Michael Witzel, he held posts at the University of Groningen (~2003–2005), Leiden University (~2005–2008), and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (from 2008).

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the Athenaeum (~1776–1779) and the University of Göttingen (~1779–1784), where he later served as a professor from circa 1794 to 1842.

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He served at Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1888–1899), was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1888, and was a Fellow at Balliol College (~1899–1917).

Arthur Berriedale Keith was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College under Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later working at the Colonial Office (~1901–1914) and as professor at the University of Edinburgh (~1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1893–1903), where he later served as professor extraordinarius of Iranian philology from 1919 to 1945.

Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He was educated at Bedford School (~-1857) and King's College London (~1857–1860), and subsequently served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1860 to 1880.

Arthur F. Wright worked in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard (~1937–1947), later holding posts at Stanford University (~1947–1959) and Yale University (~1959–1976) as Charles Seymour Professor of History.

Arthur Llewellyn Basham studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He held professorial posts at SOAS and the University of London (1953–1965), chaired Asian Civilizations at the Australian National University (1965–1978), and held appointments at Toronto (1978) and the Asiatic Society (1985–1986).

Arthur McKeown is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at Harvard University (~2003–2010), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil and Diana L. Eck, and also studied under Palri Sangye.

Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Ernestinum Gotha (1807), the University of Göttingen (1809), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1811). He held posts at the University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin between circa 1820 and 1831.
